dhcp.thePoolOfIpAddresses: The pool of IP addresses your router hands out to guest devices, plus their gateway, DNS and how long each address is held.
dhcp.perRouterDhcpAddressPools: Per-router DHCP address pools, gateway, DNS and lease time. Apply a pool to send it to the router.
dhcp.theRouterThisRangeBelongs: The router this range belongs to cannot be changed — delete it and make a new one to move it.
dhcp.theRouterThisPoolBelongs: The router this pool belongs to cannot be changed — delete and recreate to move it.
dhcp.anAddressRangeBelongsTo: An address range belongs to exactly one router for its whole life.
dhcp.aDhcpPoolBelongsTo: A DHCP pool belongs to exactly one router for its whole lifetime.
dhcp.name: Name
dhcp.couldnTApplyThisPool: Couldn't apply this pool to your router:
dhcp.noAddressRangesMatchYour: No address ranges match your filters.
dhcp.noDhcpPoolsMatchYour: No DHCP pools match your filters.
dhcp.gatewayRequired: Required — the DHCP server won't start on the router without it

vlan.couldnTApplyVlanTo: Couldn't apply VLAN {{vlanId}} to the router
vlan.splitYourNetworkIntoSeparate: Split your network into separate zones — e.g. guest Wi-Fi kept apart from staff or office devices — each with its own address range.
vlan.perRouterVlanInventoryA: Per-router VLAN inventory — a real 802.1Q tag, gateway, and CIDR record. Apply pushes a VLAN to the router; each row's badge shows what the device is holding.
vlan.theRouterThisVlanBelongs: The router this VLAN belongs to cannot be changed — delete and recreate to move it.
vlan.aVlanBelongsToExactly: A VLAN belongs to exactly one router for its whole lifetime.
vlan.takeAWholePortFor: Take a whole port for this zone (untagged)
vlan.readLiveOffYourRouter: Read live off your router. This zone rides the cable that is already there, tagged — nothing else on that cable is disturbed. Use this for several Wi-Fi networks from one access point; the AP must tag this zone's VLAN id.
vlan.nothingOnThisRouterCan: Nothing on this router can carry a tagged zone. Type a name in if you know it.
vlan.readLiveOffYourRouter2: Read live off your router. This port is handed entirely to this zone, untagged. Whatever is plugged into it leaves its current network — including an access point, which would stop serving the Wi-Fi it serves today.
vlan.noneOfThisRouterS: None of this router's ports belong to a bridge, and an access port has to. Add the port to the bridge on the router first, or use Trunk instead.
vlan.anyoneJoiningThisZoneSees: Anyone joining this zone sees your sign-in screen before they get online.
vlan.guestsOnThisVlanMust: Guests on this VLAN must log in through a hotspot page.
vlan.letDevicesInThisZone: Let devices in this zone out to the internet. Turn it off for a zone that should only see your own network — cameras or card readers, say.
vlan.typedByHandIfThis: Typed by hand — if this doesn't match the router exactly, applying the zone will fail.
vlan.couldnTApplyThisVlan: Couldn't apply this VLAN to your router:
vlan.errTrunk: Pick the interface this zone runs on — the router can't create it without one
vlan.errAccess: Pick the port to hand over to this zone
vlan.removeBody: This permanently removes "{{name}}" from {{router}}. This cannot be undone.
vlan.notOnRouter: · not on this router right now
vlan.takePortConfirm: Yes, take {{port}} out of {{bridge}}. Without this the router refuses the change.
vlan.takePortWarning: Anything plugged into that port loses the network it is on today. If an access point is on it, the Wi-Fi it serves stops working until the port is put back. Choose {{trunk}} instead to add this zone without taking the port.
vlan.portalCreatesDhcp: The sign-in page also creates this zone's {{what}}, so devices get an address automatically.
vlan.networkOnly: This creates the network only — {{what}}, so devices will join and get nothing until you create an {{pool}} with Interface set to {{iface}}.

portForwarding.perRouterNatRulesMapping: Per-router NAT rules mapping a public destination port to an internal address/port. Apply a rule to send it to the router.
portForwarding.theRouterThisRuleBelongs: The router this rule belongs to cannot be changed — delete and recreate to move it.
portForwarding.aPortForwardingRuleBelongs: A port forwarding rule belongs to exactly one router.
portForwarding.couldnTApplyThisRule: Couldn't apply this rule to your router:
portForwarding.noPortForwardingRulesMatch: No port forwarding rules match your filters.
portForwarding.removeBody: This permanently removes this port forwarding rule from {{router}}. This cannot be undone.

qos.callPriorityIntro: Send voice and video calls ahead of other guest traffic when the network is busy. This changes the order traffic is sent in; it cannot add capacity your internet line does not have.
qos.trafficClassificationRulesMatchVoice: Traffic-classification rules — match voice signaling/media (or a raw DSCP value) and assign a real RouterOS queue priority.
qos.matchTrafficByAPort: Match traffic by a port range (e.g. SIP 5060/5061) or by a raw DSCP value — never both.
qos.noQosRulesMatchYour: No QoS rules match your filters.
qos.removeBody: This permanently removes this QoS rule from {{router}}. This cannot be undone.
qos.errPortRange: Enter a valid port range (start ≤ end)

common.cannotUndo: This permanently removes it from {{router}}. This cannot be undone.
